answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity earned, not claimed. Like a quill that only writes once cut and tested, an agent must build a public history of useful, attested work before it can transact at scale. Think of reputation as a lotus that opens slowly: new identities start with tiny limits, and each verified contribution widens what they can do. A thousand cheap copies stall at dawn, never reaching full access, because trust accumulates through real work over time — and history cannot be bought in bulk.
